records.source: Διὸ μηκέτι στέγοντες εὐδοκήσαμεν καταλειφθῆναι ἐν Ἀθήναις μόνοι, καὶ ἐπέμψαμεν Τιμόθεον, τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν καὶ συνεργὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλέσαι ὑπὲρ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν τὸ μηδένα σαίνεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν ταύταις.
records.gloss: Therefore no longer bearing [it] we thought it good to be left behind in Athens alone, \v 2 and we sent Timothy, the brother of us and fellow worker of the God in the gospel of the Christ, so as to strengthen you and to encourage [you] concerning the faith of you, \v 3 so that no one be shaken in the afflictions these.
pieces: So, when we could not bear the waiting any longer, we decided to stay behind in Athens on our own
and sent you Timothy, our brother and God's fellow worker in the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. We sent him to make you strong and to encourage you in your faith,
so that none of you would be shaken by these troubles.

L.1: Therefore, when we could bear it no longer, we thought it good to be left behind in Athens alone,
L.2: and we sent Timothy, our brother and God's fellow worker in the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to strengthen you and encourage [you] in your faith,
L.3: so that no one would be shaken by these afflictions.

R.1: We could not wait any longer to hear about you. So we decided to stay in Athens by ourselves,
R.2: and we sent Timothy to you. He is our brother, and he works with God to spread the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. We sent him to make your faith strong and to encourage you,
R.3: so that none of you would give up because of these troubles.

decisions.choice: Athens: where Paul went after leaving Macedonia
decisions.reason: Driven from Thessalonica and then Berea, Paul went on to Athens (Acts 17:13-16). From there he sent Timothy back to Thessalonica; Acts tells the story more briefly and does not mention this journey.

decisions.choice: bear: hold out under the strain of not knowing
decisions.reason: στέγω means to bear or endure. What they could no longer bear was being cut off from news of the church (verse 5).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God's fellow worker"
alternatives: "a servant and fellow worker of God"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ widely here. "God's fellow worker" is a bold phrase (compare 1 Corinthians 3:9), and the other readings look like attempts to soften it or to combine them. The SBLGNT reads it, with some early support. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: be shaken: be unsettled and drawn away
alternatives: be beguiled, flattered (the word is used of a dog wagging its tail)
decisions.reason: σαίνομαι is a rare word. It first meant a dog wagging its tail, and so to fawn on or to beguile; it later came to mean to be disturbed or shaken. Either way, Paul feared that the troubles would draw them away from the faith.

decisions.choice: to strengthen and encourage you in your faith
decisions.reason: στηρίξαι and παρακαλέσαι both point to their faith: Timothy was to steady it and to urge them on.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: We could not wait any longer to hear about you; give up because of these troubles
alternatives: no longer bearing it; be shaken in these afflictions
decisions.reason: Readable says what they could not bear and what being shaken would mean (m2, m4).

records.heading: Timothy sent to strengthen them

records.source: αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο κείμεθα·
records.gloss: Yourselves for you know that for this we are appointed;
pieces: You know yourselves that we are appointed for this.

L.3: For you yourselves know that we are destined for this.

R.3: You know that God's people will have troubles like these. It is part of God's plan for us.

decisions.choice: we are appointed: placed here by God for this
decisions.reason: κεῖμαι means to lie or be set somewhere, and so to be appointed (Philippians 1:16, "I am put here for the defense of the gospel"). Trouble is part of the calling of God's people, not a sign that God has left them.

decisions.choice: for this: for afflictions
decisions.reason: εἰς τοῦτο points back to "these afflictions" in the sentence before. "We" includes all believers.

decisions.choice: God's people will have troubles like these. It is part of God's plan for us.
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this" is and who appoints it (m1, m2).

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἦμεν, προελέγομεν ὑμῖν ὅτι μέλλομεν θλίβεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ ἐγένετο καὶ οἴδατε.
records.gloss: And indeed when with you we were, we were telling you beforehand that we are about to be afflicted, just as also it happened and you know.
pieces: Even while we were with you, we told you again and again that we were bound to suffer, and it has come about, as you know.

L.4: For indeed, when we were with you, we kept telling you beforehand that we were going to suffer affliction, just as it has happened, and you know [it].

R.4: When we were with you, we told you many times that we would suffer. And you know that this is what happened.

decisions.choice: we kept telling you beforehand
decisions.reason: προελέγομεν is in the imperfect: Paul warned them more than once.

decisions.choice: were going to: were bound to
decisions.reason: μέλλω with the infinitive speaks of what is sure to happen.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο κἀγὼ μηκέτι στέγων ἔπεμψα εἰς τὸ γνῶναι τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν, μή πως ἐπείρασεν ὑμᾶς ὁ πειράζων καὶ εἰς κενὸν γένηται ὁ κόπος ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Because of this I also, no longer bearing [it], sent in order to know the faith of you, lest somehow tempted you the tempter and in vain become the labor of us.
pieces: So I too, unable to wait any longer, sent Timothy to learn how your faith was standing. I feared the tempter might somehow have tempted you, and our hard work would have come to nothing.

L.5: For this reason I also, when I could bear it no longer, sent to learn about your faith, for fear that somehow the tempter had tempted you and our labor would turn out to be in vain.

R.5: That is why I could not wait any longer. I sent Timothy to find out if you still had faith. I was afraid that Satan, who tempts people, had tempted you to give up. Then all our hard work would have been wasted.

decisions.choice: I also: Paul speaks for himself
decisions.reason: κἀγὼ moves from "we" to "I": Paul's own longing for news, as in 2:18.

decisions.choice: the tempter: Satan
decisions.reason: ὁ πειράζων is a title for Satan, who hindered Paul (2:18) and tests God's people (Matthew 4:3).

decisions.choice: for fear that he had tempted you and our labor would be in vain
decisions.reason: The first verb is past (ἐπείρασεν): had it already happened? The second looks ahead (γένηται): would the work be lost?

decisions.choice: sent Timothy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one Paul sent (verse 2).

decisions.choice: Satan, who tempts people
decisions.reason: Readable names the tempter (m2).

records.source: Ἄρτι δὲ ἐλθόντος Τιμοθέου πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ εὐαγγελισαμένου ἡμῖν τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ὑμῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἔχετε μνείαν ἡμῶν ἀγαθὴν πάντοτε ἐπιποθοῦντες ἡμᾶς ἰδεῖν καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς, διὰ τοῦτο παρεκλήθημεν, ἀδελφοί, ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ ἀνάγκῃ καὶ θλίψει ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν πίστεως, ὅτι νῦν ζῶμεν ἐὰν ὑμεῖς στήκετε ἐν κυρίῳ.
records.gloss: Now but having come Timothy to us from you and having brought good news to us of the faith and the love of you, and that you have remembrance of us good always, longing us to see just as also we you, \v 7 because of this we were encouraged, brothers, over you in all the distress and affliction of us through the your faith, \v 8 because now we live if you stand firm in [the] Lord.
pieces: But Timothy has just come back to us from you, with the good news of your faith and love. He tells us that you always remember us kindly and long to see us, as we long to see you.
So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, in all our distress and trouble your faith has given us comfort about you.
Now we can truly live again, if you are standing firm in the Lord.

L.6: But now that Timothy has come to us from you and has brought us the good news of your faith and love, and that you always have a good remembrance of us, longing to see us just as we also [long to see] you,
L.7: for this reason, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we were comforted about you in all our distress and affliction through your faith;
L.8: for now we live, if you stand firm in [the] Lord.

R.6: But Timothy has just come back from you. He brought us good news about your faith and your love. He told us that you always think of us kindly, and that you want to see us as much as we want to see you.
R.7: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we have many troubles and hard times, but your faith has encouraged us.
R.8: Now we feel truly alive, because you are standing strong in your life with the Lord.

decisions.choice: Timothy's return: Paul writes soon after it
decisions.reason: Acts 18:5 says Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia to Paul in Corinth. The letter was most likely written there, shortly after Timothy arrived.

decisions.choice: brought good news: the verb used for preaching the gospel
decisions.reason: εὐαγγελίζω usually means to preach the gospel; here it is used of Timothy's report. To Paul, news of their faith and love was itself good news.

decisions.choice: our distress and affliction: Paul's own troubles where he was
decisions.reason: ἀνάγκῃ and θλίψει are Paul's hardships, probably in Corinth (Acts 18:6, 18:12-17).

decisions.choice: now we live, if you stand firm: their steadiness is life to Paul
decisions.reason: ἐὰν ("if") is used with a present indicative, στήκετε: Paul speaks with confidence that they are standing firm, and also urges them to keep doing so.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: you are standing strong in your life with the Lord
alternatives: you stand firm in the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what standing firm "in the Lord" means.

records.heading: Timothy's good news

records.source: τίνα γὰρ εὐχαριστίαν δυνάμεθα τῷ θεῷ ἀνταποδοῦναι περὶ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ χαρᾷ ᾗ χαίρομεν δι’ ὑμᾶς ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν, νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ δεόμενοι εἰς τὸ ἰδεῖν ὑμῶν τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ καταρτίσαι τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: What for thanksgiving are we able to the God to give back concerning you for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before the God of us, \v 10 night and day beyond all measure praying for the to see of you the face and to supply the lacking things of the faith of you?
pieces: What thanks can we give back to God for you, for all the joy we feel before our God because of you?
Night and day we pray with great urgency to see you face to face and to fill in whatever is still missing from your faith.

L.9: For what thanks can we give back to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God,
L.10: night and day praying beyond all measure to see your face and to supply what is lacking in your faith?

R.9: We cannot thank God enough for you! When we pray to God, we are so full of joy because of you.
R.10: Day and night we pray very hard that we can see you again. We want to help your faith grow in the ways it still needs to grow.

decisions.choice: what thanks can we give back: no thanks could be enough
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer: the joy God has given them is more than any thanks can repay.

decisions.choice: beyond all measure: as earnestly as possible
decisions.reason: ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ is a word Paul builds up from three parts, "over, out of, beyond": the most intense way to say "exceedingly" (also 5:13).

decisions.choice: supply what is lacking: make complete, put in order
decisions.reason: καταρτίζω means to complete or mend (it is used of mending nets, Mark 1:19). Their faith is real but young; chapters 4-5 give some of the teaching it still needs.

decisions.choice: before our God: in prayer
decisions.reason: Paul's joy is expressed as he stands before God in prayer (1:3).

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable close the question at the end of verse 9
decisions.reason: The Greek question runs through verse 10; English reads more easily with the prayer as its own sentence.

decisions.choice: help your faith grow in the ways it still needs to grow
alternatives: supply what is lacking in your faith
decisions.reason: Readable avoids suggesting their faith is faulty (m3).

records.source: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς κατευθύναι τὴν ὁδὸν ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς·
records.gloss: Himself now the God and Father of us and the Lord of us Jesus may direct the way of us to you;
pieces: Now may our God and Father {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, and our Lord Jesus, clear the way for us to come to you.

L.11: Now may our God and Father {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and our Lord Jesus direct our way to you.

R.11: We pray that God our Father {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and our Lord Jesus will make a way for us to come and see you.

decisions.choice: God and Jesus act together: two subjects, one singular verb
decisions.reason: κατευθύναι ("may he direct") is singular, though God the Father and the Lord Jesus are both its subject. Paul speaks of them acting as one (compare 2 Thessalonians 2:16-17).

decisions.choice: direct our way: open the road
decisions.reason: κατευθύνω means to make a path straight. It answers the hindrance of 2:18.

decisions.choice: clear the way
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the answer to the blocked road of 2:18 (m2).

records.source: ὑμᾶς δὲ ὁ κύριος πλεονάσαι καὶ περισσεύσαι τῇ ἀγάπῃ εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας, καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς, εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας ἀμέμπτους ἐν ἁγιωσύνῃ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: You now the Lord may make increase and abound in the love toward one another and toward all, just as also we toward you, \v 13 so as to strengthen of you the hearts blameless in holiness before the God and Father of us at the coming of the Lord of us Jesus with all the holy [ones] of him.
pieces: As for you, may the Lord fill you to overflowing with love for each other and for all people, the kind of love we have for you.
Then your hearts will stand firm, without fault and holy before our God and Father when our Lord Jesus comes with all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones.

L.12: And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all, just as we also [do] for you,
L.13: so as to strengthen your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones.

R.12: And we pray that the Lord will help you love each other and everyone else more and more, the way we love you.
R.13: We pray that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make your hearts strong, so that you will be holy and no one can blame you for anything. Then you will be ready to stand before God our Father when our Lord Jesus comes back with all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: As in verses 11 and 13, "the Lord" is Jesus.

decisions.choice: for one another and for all: love that reaches beyond the church
decisions.reason: εἰς πάντας takes in everyone, including those who oppose them (5:15).

decisions.choice: blameless in holiness
decisions.reason: ἁγιωσύνῃ is holiness, being set apart for God. The theme of holiness runs into chapter 4 (4:3-8).

decisions.choice: with all his holy ones: Zechariah 14:5, "the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him"
alternatives: with all his people who have died
decisions.reason: The words echo Zechariah 14:5, where "holy ones" are probably angels, and Jesus speaks of coming with the angels (Mark 8:38). But in this letter "holy" is a word for believers, and 4:14 says God will bring with Jesus those who have died. Paul may include both.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
alternatives: "... with all his holy ones. Amen."
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "Amen" at the end of the prayer.

decisions.choice: fill you to overflowing
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the two verbs of growing and overflowing into one picture.

decisions.choice: you will be ready to stand before
decisions.reason: Readable says what being blameless "before" God means here.
